properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js@1.1.3 ships the SHA-1/SHA-2 family and is resolved in this repo's yarn.lock (pulled in via the web3/ethereumjs dependency tree); no first-party call site in packages/, so its algorithms are reachable only through that tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Real SHA-1 in use: the dashboard fingerprints each Compilation object with object-hash's sha1 — server-side at DashboardServer.ts:142 (per the comment there, hashing is done on the server because it crashes the browser) and client-side at DashProvider.tsx:108. The digests serve as decoder cache keys for change detection, a non-security purpose, but these are genuine SHA-1 operations on every compilation fetched.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency chain: node-forge 1.3.1 ← selfsigned@2.1.1 (yarn.lock:19701) ← webpack-dev-server@4.15.1 (yarn.lock:22414), the dev-HTTPS tooling for the dashboard dev server. node-forge's RSA generates the throwaway self-signed dev certificate keypair. No first-party RSA call site exists in workspace source; production browser bundles do not ship it. Changeable only by bumping webpack-dev-server.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: createMessage() mints a message-correlation ID for the local dashboard message bus (CLI ↔ dashboard browser tab over WebSocket on localhost). Math.random() is predictable and collision-prone, so an ID could in principle be guessed/replayed on the local bus, but no secret, token, or key material depends on it — weak-RNG posture finding with low security relevance. Contrast: analytics unique IDs elsewhere use uuid v4 (CSPRNG).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive: tweetnacl 0.14.5 ← sshpk@1.16.1 (tweetnacl "~0.14.0", yarn.lock:20372) and bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2 (yarn.lock:7447) — the legacy http-signature/request chain in dev tooling. Ed25519 is tweetnacl's signing capability for OpenSSH Ed25519 keys; no first-party call site in workspace code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.5.4 (ECDSA over secp256k1/secp256r1 etc.) resolved in yarn.lock; reachable through the web3/ethereumjs transitive tree at runtime; no first-party elliptic call site in packages/.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.5.4 is the pure-JS EC engine reached via secp256k1@4.0.3 (direct dep of @truffle/hdwallet, dep line yarn.lock:19675), via browserify-sign/create-ecdh in the crypto-browserify browser shim, and via ethers@4 (yarn.lock:11054). First-party EC usage here is secp256k1 public-key derivation and transaction signing; elliptic's ECDH capability ships with the library (available in the shipped build, no first-party ECDH call site).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5 resolved in yarn.lock (also tweetnacl@^1.0.3 present). X25519 (crypto_box_beforenm key agreement / scalarMult) is available to any code in the shipped tree; no first-party tweetnacl call site in packages/. Quantum-vulnerable key agreement if used by a dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: js-scrypt@^0.2.0 is declared in the truffle package's package.json:58 and aliased ("scrypt": "js-scrypt") in webpack.config.js:180 for browser builds — i.e. some bundled dependency performs require("scrypt") at runtime, which webpack resolves to js-scrypt. The password-based KDF is therefore present in the shipped bundle; no first-party scrypt(...) call site exists in packages/.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Both sites are the BIP32 HD-wallet derivation in @truffle/hdwallet, feeding @truffle/core's mnemonic accounts and @truffle/hdwallet-provider: line 37 derives the master key/chain code from the BIP39 seed with the standard "Bitcoin seed" HMAC key (a public BIP32 spec constant, not a secret); line 127 derives each child key from the parent chain code. HMAC-SHA512 itself is unbroken and PQ-relevant only via Grover's square-root on the 512-bit digest.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes 1.1.2 is the hash engine of ethereum-cryptography@1.1.2 (direct runtime dep of @truffle/hdwallet, @truffle/core, @truffle/hdwallet-provider). SHA-256 backs BIP39 mnemonic checksums and the @scure/bip32/bip39 key-derivation chain the wallet packages use. Actively reachable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 ships in @noble/hashes' module surface; no first-party BLAKE3 call site found in workspace source. Available in the shipped dependency — the standard provider-inventory entry; no action beyond noting presence.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256/SHA-3 via noble under ethereum-cryptography/keccak is THE Ethereum address primitive: @truffle/hdwallet/src/index.ts:1 imports keccak256 to derive addresses from secp256k1 public keys, and keccak-based hashing runs throughout the codec/debugger packages. Actively used, quantum-safe hash.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5's secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305 AE) resolved in yarn.lock; no first-party call site in packages/, so the AE cipher is only reachable through the transitive tree (e.g. web3-provider-engine hooked subproviders historically used crypto_box).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: selfsigned@^2.1.1 (runtime self-signed X.509 cert generation, RSA/elliptic keys) resolved in yarn.lock. Notable posture fact: this tree itself opens no TLS sessions (tls_sessions scan: none) and no first-party selfsigned call site exists in packages/, so any self-signed certs would come from a dependency's runtime behavior.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge's X.509/PKI machinery is what selfsigned@2.1.1 (← webpack-dev-server@4.15.1) uses to mint the localhost self-signed certificate for dev HTTPS. Dev tooling only; no first-party certificate handling in the application. Related: the "X.509 self-signed" algorithm object (other shard) covers the certificate-generation angle of the same chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Node's crypto.randomBytes(16) supplies the 128-bit entropy for the BIP39 mnemonic generated in getOrGenerateMnemonic() — the master secret backing Truffle's default Ethereum accounts. Strong CSPRNG, correctly used. Posture note recorded in the hunt summary: the generated mnemonic is then persisted in cleartext to the user's truffle config (defaultUserConfig.set({ mnemonic }), line 34).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory anchor for the tweetnacl Ed25519 object: tweetnacl 0.14.5 ships Ed25519 signing, X25519, and NaCl box/secretbox; it is deep dev tooling here (sshpk/bcrypt-pbkdf via the legacy request chain), not reachable from application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js 2.0.4 is pinned by ethers@4.0.49 (yarn.lock:11057) — the legacy ethers v4 keystore/scrypt path that @truffle/contract and @truffle/interface-adapter pull in via their ethers ^4.0.32 runtime deps (contract signs transactions through ethers.Wallet). The newer scrypt-js 3.0.1 sits under @ethersproject/json-wallets and ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3. scrypt is a quantum-safe KDF.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1/SHA-2 stream-hash provider. Requested by pbkdf2 ("^2.4.8", yarn.lock:9054) and create-hash ("^2.4.0", yarn.lock:9042) — i.e. it ships inside the crypto-browserify browser bundles of @truffle/contract (browser-dist/truffle-contract.js) and the dashboard, where any createHash('sha1'|'sha256') in bundled web3 code lands on sha.js.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The elliptic 6.5.4 library object backing the ECDH algorithm object: reached via secp256k1@4.0.3 (hdwallet), browserify-sign/create-ecdh (crypto-browserify browser shim), ethers@4 and @ethersproject/signing-key (ethers 5, direct dep of @truffle/dashboard). ECDSA secp256k1 transaction signing in packages/contract/lib/manual-send.js runs through this engine.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The crypto engine of ethereum-cryptography@1.1.2, a direct runtime dependency of @truffle/hdwallet, @truffle/core and @truffle/hdwallet-provider (SHA-2, SHA-3/Keccak, BLAKE, ripemd, pbkdf2, scrypt surfaces). The single most load-bearing crypto dependency in the repo; version 1.1.2 predates the noble-hashes SHA-3 fixes but nothing here depends on those.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned 2.1.1 ← webpack-dev-server@4.15.1 (yarn.lock:22414): mints the self-signed X.509 certificate (RSA keypair via node-forge) that lets the dashboard dev server serve HTTPS on localhost. Dev tooling only; not shipped in any production bundle. Changeable by bumping webpack-dev-server.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js 1.1.3 is pinned by ethers@4.0.49 (the runtime dep of @truffle/contract and @truffle/interface-adapter, used for transaction signing); 1.1.7 arrives via elliptic@6.5.4 (yarn.lock:10086) and @ethersproject/signing-key (ethers 5, direct dep of @truffle/dashboard). Provides SHA-256/RIPEMD-160 used in Ethereum key hashing inside the shipped signing path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same asset as the PBKDF2 algorithm object: the pbkdf2 npm package, requested by ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 (web3 1.10 stack) and crypto-browserify@3.12.0 (browser shim in @truffle/contract's and the dashboard's bundles). Dependency-inventory anchor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge 1.3.1 is the PKI/crypto backend of selfsigned (dev HTTPS certs via webpack-dev-server). It ships RSA, AES, X.509, MD5/SHA-1 and PKCS#7/12 machinery — all confined to dev tooling in this repo; no first-party import of node-forge exists in workspace source.
